hero.headline: Be a rancher without leaving home.
hero.releaseRule: Your own herd in the Paraguayan Chaco, raised by our cowboys under the Orbolo Code. A ranch starts once 60% of its herd is committed. No money moves before then.

included: Pregnant cows, tagged in your name, on a named ranch you can visit
A life on grass and under native trees, without growth hormones or antibiotic promoters
A report after every muster: numbers, photos and your tag list
Nothing to pay until the ranch is released
offerBox.termsOnRequestNote: Herd size, cycle length, costs and payout timing vary per ranch, and we can’t publish them here for legal reasons. They’re in the Remote Rancher pack, on request.

isThisReal.elTapirIntro: Yes. El Tapir is the group’s own farm in the Gran Chaco. Not a partner ranch: ours. The first Remote Rancher herd lives there, and it hasn’t closed a full cycle yet. Come and see it.

whoBuysAtEnd.body: Orbolo’s own trading desk, at market prices. Every herd has its buyer before it’s bought.

whatIfNotEnough.releaseRuleBody: A ranch is released only when 60% of its herd is committed under signed letters of intent. Below that, nobody pays anything.
whatIfNotEnough.loiExpiryBody: A letter of intent expires after 90 days. If the ranch isn’t at 60% by then, it stays open or is withdrawn. Either way, you’re told.

categories.label: Animal loss
categories.body: Cattle can be lost to disease, predators or accidents.

categories.label: Drought
categories.body: A dry year means fewer calves. The herd is built to hold through it.

categories.label: Currency
categories.body: On the ground, money moves in guaraníes, and exchange rates move too.

categories.label: Policy and export
categories.body: Export markets and trade rules can change during a cycle.

categories.label: Liquidity
categories.body: This isn’t money you can take back on short notice. A herd is committed for its whole cycle.

whatIfWrong.dataRoomNote: How each risk is handled is set out in the full data room, open once you sign an NDA.

steps.body: Choose a ranch from the pipeline.
Read the Remote Rancher pack, then open the full data room under NDA.
Sign a letter of intent. It’s non-binding, and nothing is paid.
At 60% committed, the ranch is released.
Only then do you sign with our Paraguayan operating company and pay. Your cows arrive by truck and are tagged in your name.
Cowboys raise them on pasture under the Orbolo Code, all year round.
At the muster, the calves are sold through Orbolo’s trading desk at market prices, and you’re paid your share.

whatYouOwn.body: Specific cows, by ear tag, under a management agreement with our Paraguayan operating company. Not land, and not a share in a fund. Carbon or biodiversity credits stay with the land and the group.

whoVerifies.codeReferenceNote: Every animal is raised under the Orbolo Code: room to move, shade, water, no growth hormones.

items.question: Do I need to visit Paraguay to own cattle here?
items.answer: No. Your reports bring the ranch to your desk. But you’re very welcome, by appointment.

items.question: How do I know the animals actually exist?
items.answer: Every cow carries an ear tag and a digital tag, both on your list. The details are in the Remote Rancher pack.

items.question: Can I leave early?
items.answer: Not today. A herd is committed for its cycle. Ask us about your situation.

items.question: Who can become a Remote Rancher?
items.answer: That depends on where you live, among other things. Contact us to find out if you’re eligible.

items.question: What happens when the cycle ends?
items.answer: The animals are sold through Orbolo’s trading desk at market prices, and you’re paid your share.

closing.releaseLine: Released at 60%. Nothing paid before then.
